children: A former Motley Rice attorney has been sentenced to more than seven years in prison for defrauding the prominent plaintiffs' law firm out of more than $2 million through fictitious companies and false settlement claims.

US District Judge Richard Gergel in Charleston, South Carolina, on Monday sentenced William Christopher Swett to 87 months in prison and ordered him to pay more than $2.5 million in restitution. Swett, 42, pleaded guilty to four counts of wire fraud and four counts of money laundering in February.
“Swett abused his position of trust that he held with both his law firm and his clients,” South Carolina US Attorney Bryan Stirling said in a statement.
Nathan Williams, a Mount Pleasant, South Carolina-based attorney who represented Swett, said his client realized he must be held accountable for his actions, and tried to do his best to make amends.
"Once it became clear to him that he couldn’t keep living that way, he took accountability," Williams said.

According to prosecutors, Swett profited for five years from two fictitious legal services companies he secretly created that sought and received reimbursements from Motley Rice. He also filed fake personal injury claims for family members and routed the proceeds to bank accounts he controlled, prosecutors said.

Swett was a lawyer at South Carolina-based Motley Rice for 12 years and eventually admitted to the scheme to Motley Rice, according to court papers Williams filed on his behalf last week. Williams in an interview and in court papers said Swett had a severe gambling addiction and substance abuse issues.

"Gambling consumed every financial avenue available to Mr. Swett and contributed to his decision to steal after his personal resources were exhausted," Williams wrote last week in a brief that asked for a shorter prison sentence.
A spokesperson for Motley Rice did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
